title: Cobalt — handoff scratch & ephemeral runbook
content:
Quick note: this is a scratch/handoff doc — do not paste secrets here.

SHIFT SUMMARY (start 2025-03-01 23:00 PT -> end 2025-03-02 07:00 PT)
- Primary for shift: Maya K. Singh (me). Follow: Evan (first 2 hrs), Lina (last 3 hrs).
- Quiet overall, two small items: one transient latency spike at ~01:10 and a cache churn event at ~03:40 that I mitigated with a temporary TTL bump.
- No open P1s at handoff. Leaving a few follow-ups (see below).

CURRENT SYSTEM STATE (high-level)
- Hosted API: green. Error rate steady at ~0.03% on production routes.
- Dedicated pools: 1/3 nodes in pool-alpha showing elevated GPU mem high water (spikes during long-context jobs).
- Redis prefix-cache: eviction rate spiked between 03:30-03:45 -> caused increased token-generation cost for a small cohort.
- Fallback routing: saw 12 automatic fallbacks to model-compat variants between 01:00-02:00 due to transient scheduler latency. Observed ~120ms added latency on those requests.

INCIDENTS / NOTES (chrono)
- 2025-03-02 01:10: latency-blip-01 (transient)
  - Symptom: p50->p90 jump on /v1/generate for route 'chatty-bot' (p95 ~1.2s -> 2.7s for 4m). No errors.
  - Quick triage: looked at autoscaler logs (k8s HPA) — correlated with a small surge from one client sending many short messages.
  - Mitigation: temporarily adjusted per-route concurrency throttle from 50 -> 35 to protect downstream KV store. Throttle reverted automatically at 01:20.
  - Notes: raised a follow-up to product to add a per-client rate-limit flag for heavy short-message workloads (OPS-342).

- 2025-03-02 03:40: redis-eviction-churn
  - Symptom: cache miss rate up 8x for embed-prefix-cache, Redis memory usage bumped to 92%. Evictions visible.
  - Quick triage: background re-index job (daily batch) started earlier than expected due to cron drift on worker-2. That triggered a lot of large prefix writes.
  - Mitigation performed: bumped prefix cache TTLs for non-critical prefixes (temporary) and disabled the re-index cron on worker-2 (manual cronstop + ticket to cron team).
  - Commands I ran (notes):
    - kubectl -n infra exec deploy/redis-primary -- redis-cli INFO MEMORY | sed -n '1,30p'
    - REDIS_KEYS=$(kubectl -n infra exec deploy/redis-primary -- redis-cli --scan --pattern "prefix:*" | wc -l)
    - kubectl -n infra exec deploy/redis-primary -- redis-cli CONFIG SET maxmemory 10gb
  - Caveat: increased maxmemory is temporary; please revert once re-index job moved to offpeak.

HEALTH CHECKS TO RUN ON TAKEOVER (short):
- curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/health | jq .routes | grep -A2 chatty-bot
- kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=model-server -o wide  # check node restarts/ooms
- kubectl -n infra exec deploy/redis-primary -- redis-cli INFO | egrep 'used_memory_human|evicted_keys|instantaneous_ops_per_sec'
- curl -sS https://console.redwood.ai/metrics?q=latency&p90
- grep -i "fallback" /var/log/serving/runtime/*.log | tail -n 100

QUICK TROUBLESHOOT PLAYBOOKS (ephemeral, for common things)
1) Model server OOM / high GPU mem (fast triage)\   - Symptoms: pod restarts, GPU mem approaching 100%, large GSUtil jobs or long-context runs correlated.\   - Quick checks: nvidia-smi (inside pod), kubectl describe pod -> look for OOMKilled, dmesg for out-of-memory.\   - Temporary mitigations:\     - cordon node if multiple pods thrash: kubectl cordon <node>\     - scale down concurrent replicas for that deployment: kubectl scale deploy/<model> --replicas=1\     - enable fallback routing for that model to cheaper-variant: rctl route set --route <route> --fallback model-compat-v2\   - Follow-up: open GH issue with model owner, include trace + token counts
\2) Sudden spike of fallbacks (scheduler latency)\   - Symptoms: increase in fallback counts, higher p95 on affected route, scheduler controller logs show 'slow-schedule' warnings.\   - Triaged by: check scheduler pod latency, controller-manager logs.\   - Temp action: increase scheduling window to 250ms (serving-scheduler config) and re-evaluate. Use observability to watch delta.
\3) Redis eviction loop (what I did)\   - Symptoms: eviction_count rising, useful prefix misses.\   - Steps:\     - Pause any large batch jobs (cron team), bump temp maxmemory if safe, bump TTL for non-critical keys, move heavy writes to dedup queue.\     - Useful command: kubectl -n infra exec deploy/redis-primary -- redis-cli INFO MEMORY | egrep 'evicted_keys|used_memory'

TEMPORARY SCRIPTS / SNIPPETS (save for next oncall)
- quick-cache-flush-for-route.sh  (do NOT run in prod without approval)\  # sample snippet for local testing only
  #!/bin/bash
  ROUTE=$1
  for k in $(kubectl -n infra exec deploy/redis-primary -- redis-cli --scan --pattern "prefix:${ROUTE}:*"); do
    kubectl -n infra exec deploy/redis-primary -- redis-cli DEL "$k"
  done

- list-high-gpu-pods.sh
  kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=model-server -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount} {.spec.nodeName}\n{end}' | column -t

FOLLOW-UPS (to leave for next shift)
- Ticket OPS-342 (rate-limit flag) assigned to Evan — needs product scoping.
- Re-index cron: follow up with infra-cron team to schedule to 03:00-04:00 UTC only (was drifted). Lina owning the coordination.
- Revert temporary Redis maxmemory bump after cron is moved and eviction rate returns to baseline. (I set a calendar reminder 2025-03-03 to check)
- Add an automated alert to fire when eviction rate > 5/min for > 3m. (Alert draft in PagerDuty under 'redis-evictions-v2')

OPEN QUESTIONS / WISH LIST
- Can we add per-client rate-limiting at the gateway layer? (current rate-limiting is per-route only)
- Is there a safe way to snapshot and restore a subset of prefix keys to avoid heavy re-writes during re-index? (thinking: export important prefixes daily)
